title: Figaro Proximity Schema v1
description: Off-chain schema definition for the figaro-proximity-v1 attestation schema. Defines the radio-range proximity proof protocol used for physical custody-transfer verification in Figaro delivery processes. Submitted as a standard attestation alongside delivery lifecycle stages.

overview.description: Proximity proofs are challenge-response attestations that demonstrate physical co-location between a fulfiller device and a verifier device at a custody-transfer point (pickup or delivery). The proof is submitted as a separate attestation under this schema, concurrent with or immediately before the corresponding lifecycle stage (PickedUp or Delivered).
overview.onChainBinding: Proximity attestations are submitted via AttestationCoordinator.attestAsSeller. The stage field encodes the proximity band. The contentRef commits the proof payload (band, nonce, deviceSig) as keccak256(JSON.stringify({band, nonce, deviceSig})).
overview.relationToDeliveryLifecycle: A proximity attestation under figaro-proximity-v1 may accompany stage 3 (PickedUp) or stage 4 (Delivered) from figaro-delivery-lifecycle-v1. The lifecycle stage attests the logistical event; the proximity attestation independently proves physical co-location at that event.

0.name: None
0.description: No proximity signal. Reserved as a fallback stage for cases where proximity proof is submitted but the band detection failed. Not a valid proof band for custody verification — indexers should treat stage 0 as a null proof.
0.contentRefFormat: keccak256(JSON.stringify({band: 0, nonce, deviceSig})) — present but not probative.

1.name: Zone
1.description: WiFi-range proximity. Fulfiller and verifier devices are within the same WiFi broadcast zone (~30m). Provides neighbourhood-level co-location proof. Suitable for venue-level pickup confirmation where physical proximity within the premises is sufficient.
1.contentRefFormat: keccak256(JSON.stringify({band: 1, nonce, deviceSig})) where nonce is a random bytes32 and deviceSig is the verifier device's secp256k1 signature over keccak256(nonce).

2.name: Nearby
2.description: BLE-range proximity. Fulfiller and verifier devices are within Bluetooth Low Energy range (~10m). Provides room-level co-location proof. Suitable for handoff scenarios requiring tighter range confirmation than WiFi but not requiring physical contact.
2.contentRefFormat: keccak256(JSON.stringify({band: 2, nonce, deviceSig})) where nonce is a random bytes32 and deviceSig is the verifier device's secp256k1 signature over keccak256(nonce).

3.name: Contact
3.description: NFC-range proximity. Fulfiller and verifier devices are in physical contact range (~4cm). Provides physical-touch-level co-location proof. Provides the strongest proximity signal available under this schema. Suitable for high-value or high-sensitivity handoffs.
3.contentRefFormat: keccak256(JSON.stringify({band: 3, nonce, deviceSig})) where nonce is a random bytes32 and deviceSig is the verifier device's secp256k1 signature over keccak256(nonce).

proofPayload.description: The proof payload is a JSON object committed into the contentRef via keccak256. It is stored off-chain (IPFS or coordination channel) for dispute reconstruction. The on-chain contentRef is a deterministic binding — the actual payload is recoverable from the off-chain store.

fields.band: uint8 (0–3). The proximity band detected. Must match the attestation stage.
fields.nonce: bytes32 hex string. Random challenge value generated by the fulfiller device. Prevents replay.
fields.deviceSig: bytes hex string. secp256k1 signature by the verifier device over keccak256(nonce). Proves device presence.

proofPayload.encodingFunction: encodeProximityProofRef({band, nonce, deviceSig}) = keccak256(stringToHex(JSON.stringify({band, nonce, deviceSig}))). Implemented in frontend/lib/mechanisms/useDeliveryLifecycle.ts.

indexingNotes.description: Indexers reconstructing delivery evidence should correlate proximity attestations with delivery lifecycle attestations by (processId, orderHash) and block timestamp.
indexingNotes.bandHierarchy: For dispute resolution, higher band values indicate stronger proximity proof. Stage 3 (Contact) supersedes stage 2 (Nearby) supersedes stage 1 (Zone) as evidence of physical handoff.
indexingNotes.multipleProofs: Multiple proximity attestations on the same (orderHash, handoffStep) are valid. The strongest band seen is the authoritative evidence signal.
